Assessment Writing

CCSS-Aligned ELA Assessment Items

Selected response and constructed response items written to CCSS benchmarks across Grades 3–12, with full rationales and scoring rubrics.

Grades 3–5
Selected Response
Vocabulary in Context: 'Inscribed'
DOK 1 · CCSS.ELA-Literacy.L

Students determine the meaning of 'inscribed' using context from Baum's Oz series, with four carefully differentiated distractors including 'saved' and 'recorded'.

Grades 6–8
Selected Response
Capitalization: Proper Nouns
DOK 1 · CCSS.ELA-Literacy.L — Conventions

Students identify the correctly capitalized sentence from a Little Women passage, distinguishing holidays, continents, and proper nouns from common adverbs.

Grades 9–10
Selected Response
Author's Argument: Patrick Henry
DOK 1 · CCSS.ELA-Literacy.RI.9-10.5

Students analyze why Henry considers himself 'guilty of treason' in his Virginia Convention speech — distinguishing self-censorship from disagreement, with complete distractor rationales.

Grades 9–10
Selected Response
Precise Claim: G.K. Chesterton
DOK 2 · CCSS.ELA-Literacy.W.9-10.1a

Students identify the precise claim in Chesterton's 'The Fallacy of Success,' distinguishing central argument from supporting details and four carefully crafted distractors.

Grades 11–12
Selected Response
Context Clues: 'Visage' in Ozymandias
DOK 2 · CCSS.ELA-Literacy.L.11-12.4a

Students use contextual clues (sunk, sand, stone, subject of poem) to determine that 'visage' means face — with distractors (ship, crown, rock) designed around plausible misreadings.

Grades 11–12
Constructed Response
Comparing Fitzgerald & Hemingway
DOK 3 · CCSS.ELA-Literacy.RL.11-12.9

Students compare passages from The Great Gatsby and A Farewell to Arms, analyzing how post-war abundance contrasts with wartime bleakness. Includes full scoring rubric and two scored exemplars.

A Pass Educational Group — Full Assessment Writing Sample

Complete writing sample per A Pass specifications — 3 selected response + 1 constructed response, Grades 9–12, each at a different DOK level, with full rationale sets and a scored rubric with 2-point and 1-point exemplars.
